title: Pakistan Kills 48 Militants in High-Tempo 72-Hour Balochistan Operations, Including 26 in a Single Quetta Raid
detail: ISPR said security forces killed 48 militants belonging to Fitna al-Hindustan and Fitna al-Khawarij across Balochistan over 48-72 hours through September 4, 2026 — the province's largest toll since the August 21 nationwide sweep. The single largest action was in the Shaban area of Quetta district, where forces identified four militant hideouts and killed 26 fighters in an intense exchange of fire; further operations killed 6 in Mastung, 2 in Kalat and 2 in the Bagh area of Sibi district. The military said it would continue operations 'under the Azm-e-Istehkam vision until the elimination of the last terrorist.' President Asif Ali Zardari said more than 1,188 terrorists have been killed in Balochistan in 2026 alone, and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi commended the forces involved.

title: Baloch Liberation Army Claims Killing 25 Pakistani Soldiers in Ziarat Cross Convoy Ambush and Surab VBIED Attack
detail: The Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) claimed responsibility on September 4, 2026 for two attacks on Pakistani forces in Balochistan. BLA spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch said the group's Fateh Squad ambushed a four-vehicle army convoy at Ziarat Cross — the same crossing hit by a TTP attack on the customs house three days earlier — destroying two vehicles including a military truck and killing what it first said was 18 personnel, later revised upward to 25; the group claimed weapons were seized and five wounded personnel escaped. Separately, BLA's 'Special Tactical Operations Squad' said it remotely detonated an explosives-laden vehicle in the Hajika area of Surab, Kalat district, destroying an army vehicle and killing 7 soldiers. The BLA released an edited video through its Hakkal media channel showing burning military vehicles and bodies at the scene. Pakistan's ISPR had not confirmed the claimed casualty figures as of publication; the toll is disputed and unverified by independent sources.
